relationships.subject: mechanical loading
relationships.evidence_quote: We found that PGE2 levels increased at 3 and 6 h after loading and then dropped to normal levels after 12 h (Fig. 2i).

relationships.subject: COX2
relationships.evidence_quote: Moreover, we did not see an increase in bone formation in COX2Ocn−/− mice after mechanical loading (Fig. 2n, o) suggesting that mechanical loading via upregulation of PGE2 levels promotes bone formation.

relationships.subject: sensory nerve
relationships.evidence_quote: Taken together, these results indicate that peripheral sensory nerves regulate load-induced osteogenesis.

relationships.subject: EP4
relationships.evidence_quote: In the EP4wt mice, the bone mass increased significantly after mechanical loading compared to the control group, as shown by μCT analysis. However, this effect was diminished in the EP4Avil–/– mice (Fig. 4a).

relationships.subject: mechanical loading
relationships.evidence_quote: By immunostaining of hypothalamic sections, we found that mechanical loading was associated with significantly greater levels of phosphorylated CREB (pCREB) in the ARC compared with the non-loading control group (Fig. 4c).

relationships.subject: mechanical loading
relationships.evidence_quote: TH expression was significantly lower in the mechanical loading group compared to the control group (Fig. 4f).

relationships.subject: CREM
relationships.evidence_quote: found that mechanical loading induced specific binding of CREM to the CRE binding site of the Th promoter (Fig. 6f)

key_findings: Bone PGE2 (osteoblast COX2-derived) rises with mechanical loading and acts via EP4 on sensory nerves to drive bone formation.
Loading activates an ARC-to-PVN circuit (pCREB, CREM) that suppresses sympathetic TH expression to promote osteogenesis.
